summary: CLI service principal key rotation failing due to Okta group claim truncation, blocking CI pipelines
description:
Issue summary:
A recurring failure during automated CLI service principal key rotation is causing CI pipelines (Jenkins and internal GitHub Actions runners) to fail when authenticating to the internal artifact registry. Symptoms point to Okta JWT group claim being truncated when the principal is a member of a large number of groups; the truncated claim results in an unauthorized error during token exchange.

Impact:
- Multiple nightly CI jobs are failing to authenticate to the artifact registry, causing build artifacts to not be published (affects ~25 pipelines).
- Affects internal engineering teams across infra and platform services; immediate workaround requires manual key rotation and temporary token injection.

Environment:
- Affected environment: prod-us-east (identity proxy + artifact-registry + Jenkins runners)
- IdP: Okta (SCIM-managed groups + inline group claims in SAML/OIDC assertions)
- Components involved: identity-proxy, svc-token-rotator, artifact-registry-auth, jenkins-auth-plugin

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger automated key rotation for a service principal with >120 group memberships via svc-token-rotator job.
2) svc-token-rotator requests a short-lived token from identity-proxy which performs an OIDC token exchange with Okta.
3) identity-proxy receives JWT where the "groups" claim appears truncated (trailing groups missing).
4) artifact-registry enforcer rejects the token because the expected group membership check fails, returning 401 Unauthorized.

Observed behaviour:
- identity-proxy logs show a groups claim size of ~10KB and truncated JSON array.
- Okta logs show successful assertion issuance; no explicit error on Okta side.
- svc-token-rotator retries but fails; temporary manual upload token allowed builds to proceed.

Expected behaviour:
- OIDC exchange should include the full groups claim or an alternative mechanism (groups in userinfo endpoint or use group IDs) so downstream enforcers can verify membership.

Immediate workaround:
- Manual key rotation for impacted service principals with a scoped, temporary group membership reduction (remove non-essential groups) and re-run rotation. This is labor-intensive and not sustainable.

Additional notes:
- Not all service principals are affected; those with many Okta groups (>100) are most likely to hit claim size truncation thresholds.
- This ticket escalated from support chatter in #identity-support and a failing Jenkins run link in #ci-alerts.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Support (Aisha Patel): Initial report created after on-call alerted via #ci-alerts. Attached failing Jenkins job: https://jenkins.redwood/blue/organizations/jenkins/build/infra-artifact-publish/1254/

2026-03-12 10:05 - SRE (Marco Liu): Reproduced locally against a test principal with 130 groups. Observed groups claim length ~10.3KB and JSON array ends abruptly. Opening packet captures and token logs now.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Identity (Sofia Martinez): Okta introspection shows full assertion sent to our callback endpoint — suspecting a header or proxy trimming at the identity-proxy side. Asking for raw assertion captured at edge proxy.

2026-03-12 13:02 - Platform (Devon Kim): Verified artifact-registry accepts tokens with group membership expressed as group IDs in 'x-groups' header. That header not present for rotated tokens. Could be identity-proxy transformation bug.

2026-03-12 17:10 - SRE (Marco Liu): Added mitigation script to svc-token-rotator to call Okta userinfo endpoint post-exchange and attach group IDs into x-groups header before call to artifact-registry. Pushing as hotfix to staging for validation.

2026-03-13 08:44 - Identity (Sofia Martinez): Submitted an Okta support ticket to confirm maximum claim payloads expected for our assertion type and whether any intermediate proxy might be truncating body. Okta case ID: 054321-OKTA.
investigation_notes: Captured raw HTTP bodies between identity-proxy and Okta. The response from Okta includes full groups array (~12KB).
identity-proxy middleware (go HTTP server) applies a maxHeaderBytes setting set to 8192 on the listener historically; increased it temporarily in staging to 65536 to validate hypothesis.

When maxHeaderBytes increased in staging, rotated tokens contained full groups array and artifact-registry accepted the tokens. Confirms header-size limitation during identity-proxy cookie/token forwarding.

svc-token-rotator was packaging the Okta assertion into an Authorization: Bearer header for the artifact-registry call; large claims caused header truncation at the identity-proxy boundary when relaying.

Short-term mitigation: call Okta userinfo endpoint to fetch group IDs and push them in a dedicated x-groups header so downstream checks are header-size friendly. Long-term: change to reference-style group encoding or use token introspection flow with server-side lookup.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: hotfix branch added to svc-token-rotator to call userinfo and populate x-groups header. Identity-proxy listener config patched in staging to increase maxHeaderBytes to 65536 for validation. Pending deployment to prod and rollback plan. Follow-ups: (1) implement reference-style group IDs via token introspection (tracked in GH PRs), (2) add automated test for large-group principals to CI.
